record.evidence: Executive summary, Secs.3-5, 9 (pp.5-18,35): impossibility of stable SHAP rankings under collinearity; experiments on 11 datasets and a 77-dataset survey
record.problem: Retraining the same model with a different seed can invert which correlated feature SHAP ranks as most important.
record.method: Proves that no feature ranking can be faithful, stable and complete under collinearity; quantitative bounds for gradient boosting, Lasso, neural networks and random forests; DASH (ensemble-averaged SHAP) as resolution; Lean 4 formalisation (305 theorems).
record.data: Survey of 77 public datasets; experiments across 11 datasets and 3 GBDT implementations; financial case studies (p.6).
record.evaluation: Flip rates of within-group rankings, expected Spearman ranking stability, bootstrap 95% CIs over 10 trials (p.18); SNR-based flip-rate formula (R2 = 0.94 on Breast Cancer, p.35).
record.findings: 68% of 77 datasets show attribution instability; for collinear pairs the ranking is close to a coin flip; the attribution ratio diverges as 1/(1-rho^2) for gradient boosting but converges for random forests; DASH yields stable rankings (pp.5-15).
record.limitations: Authors: the result concerns the single-model paradigm; conditional SHAP does not escape it (p.7). Ours: preprint; very long theoretical document.
record.repro: Code and Lean proofs: github.com/DrakeCaraker/dash-impossibility-lean and dash-shap.
record.qa_notes: Q10 seeds/trials and CIs reported.

record.problem: Stochastic components make attribution rankings vary between runs; how far down a ranking can be trusted?
record.method: Distribution-based framework: attribution distributions over repeated runs; pairwise separability of adjacent features (continuous Jaccard distance) defines the largest reliable rank (k-stability); explainers compared by the proportion of instances where one is more stable.

record.evidence: Abstract, Secs.3-5 (pp.1-7): SHAP/LIME disagreement between prediction-equivalent models of different hypothesis classes on 24 tabular datasets, with theory
record.problem: Practice assumes that models with equivalent predictions give equivalent explanations.
record.method: Large empirical study of prediction-equivalent models from different hypothesis classes (tree-based, linear, neural); Spearman disagreement of SHAP (and LIME) vectors; Agreement Gap theorem linking disagreement to interaction density and axis-aligned tree splits (TreeSHAP interaction lemma); reliability score R(x).
record.data: 24 tabular datasets (MNIST only as a preliminary appendix extension) (pp.2,7).
record.evaluation: Lottery rate (instances with substantial disagreement, rho < 0.5), within- vs cross-class Spearman, Cohen's d; correlation with dimensionality.
record.findings: Prediction-equivalent models gave substantially different attributions; within-class rho = 1.000 vs cross-class 0.369 under split invariance; tree-linear agreement fell to 0.287 for d > 50 (r = -0.251, p < 0.001) (p.7).
record.limitations: Authors: within-neural instability not analysed (p.12). Ours: single-author preprint; disagreement across classes rather than perturbation stability.
record.repro: Reliability-score code shown in appendix; no repository link found.
record.qa_notes: Q8 code snippets only; Q10 multiple seeds controlled.

record.problem: LIME/SHAP-type explanations are unstable near decision boundaries, which is criticised in regulated credit settings.
record.method: Out-of-sample (OOS) Lipschitz and Hessian instability measures for local linear explanations and OOS Shapley values; conformal forecast-uncertainty; simulations with three data-generating functions and three model types (incl. gradient boosted trees, piecewise linear regression, sigmoid neural networks).

record.evidence: Abstract and Secs.II-IV (pp.1-8): SHAP stability under Gaussian perturbation across DEM resolutions for LR, SVM, RF and XGBoost with repeated seeds (tabular slope-unit factors)
record.problem: Whether finer input data that improve predictive accuracy also improve explanation reliability.
record.method: Ten DEM-derived conditioning factors at 1-90 m resolutions aggregated to slope units; LR, SVM, RF, XGBoost under repeated random seeds; SHAP explanations scored for faithfulness, stability (attribution distance under Gaussian perturbation) and geomorphic consistency.
record.data: Event-based landslide inventory with slope units and DEMs resampled from a 1 m GF-7 DEM (pp.4-5).
record.evaluation: AUC-type performance; faithfulness, stability and geomorphic consistency across resolutions and models.
record.findings: Predictive performance and explanation reliability did not improve together; stability responded to resolution and model, and coarse DEMs could look stable by smoothing terrain while shifting feature-importance structure (abstract; p.7).
record.limitations: Authors: single event inventory; no spatial-block validation (p.18).
record.repro: Implementation details in appendix; code not checked.
record.qa_notes: Q8 not verified; Q10 repeated seeds.
